audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the level chart disagrees with its own why text, and the whys are the ones that match the packet. content win[] reads Skill, Renekton, Renekton, Skill, Skill, Renekton, Renekton. whys[] read Darius, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Darius, Darius, Darius. The packet levelChart reads Darius, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Darius, Darius, Darius — identical to the whys. Five of the seven side tokens are wrong, including both late rows, which are printed as Renekton wins on a page whose own text says "Renekton falls off hard while you scale".
audit.why: The whys and the packet agree with each other and with the shape of the matchup: Renekton owns levels 2 through 5 on Fury, Darius owns level 1 (empty Fury bar), level 6 (Guillotine) and everything after (Renekton's single-burst pattern versus reset chaining). The 51.87% Darius win rate over 3881 games fits a chart where Darius holds four rows including all three late ones. Only the tokens were wrong.
audit.corrected: Whole chart proposed as one atomic group. win[0] Skill -> Darius, win[3] Skill -> Renekton, win[4] Skill -> Darius, win[5] Renekton -> Darius, win[6] Renekton -> Darius; win[1] and win[2] already correct. phases[0].side Skill -> Darius (5/10 -> 6.5/10), phases[1].rating 5/10 -> 4/10 and phases[2].rating 5/10 -> 3.5/10 so the numbers stop reading neutral on rows the text calls Renekton's, phases[3].side Skill -> Renekton, phases[4].side Skill -> Darius (4/10 -> 6.5/10), phases[5].side Renekton -> Darius (5/10 -> 7/10), phases[6].side Renekton -> Darius (5/10 -> 7/10). Final chart: Darius, Renekton, Renekton, Renekton, Darius, Darius, Darius.

audit.whatIsWrong: Reign of Anger generates MORE Fury the lower Renekton's health is, and the page says the opposite — spikes[1] tells the player to execute "through his low-fury state", as though a bleeding Renekton were a disarmed one.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Renekton's attacks generate Fury, increased when he is low on life." This inverts the whole Darius plan against him. Darius's pattern is the long trade that ends at five stacks, but every second of that trade past the halfway mark is refilling the bar that produces a 1.5s stun. The correct advice is the opposite of what the page says: once he is low, finish or leave, do not extend.
audit.corrected: Stated in tldr, report[0], spikes[1], whys[3], report[5], breakdown.trading and report[11].

audit.whatIsWrong: Empowered Ruthless Predator destroys damage shields, and the itemization section recommends Sterak's Gage anyway.
audit.why: Riot's text: "If Renekton has more than 50 Fury, he slashes his target three times, destroying damage shields on the target, dealing high physical damage, and stunning them for 1.5 seconds." Sterak's Gage is a damage shield. Buying it as the answer to his all-in buys a lifeline he can delete on command, which is precisely backwards. Nothing on the page mentions this.
audit.corrected: report[8] now steers to Death's Dance over Sterak's and states why; the shield-strip is also named in spikes[0], breakdown.early, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dominus grants bonus Health, which directly raises the health bar Noxian Guillotine has to execute through. The page treats level 6 as a clean Darius flip with no caveat.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Renekton transforms into the Tyrant form, gaining bonus Health and dealing damage to enemies around him. While in this form, Renekton gains Fury periodically." Two consequences the player needs: the execute threshold moves the instant he ults, so R goes before Dominus rather than after; and because he regenerates Fury passively in that form, his empowered stun is effectively always available for its duration.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[4], phases[4].why, dosFull[2].d, content.late and report[11].

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr and report[0] tell the player to "catch his escape dash mid-flight with a reactive hook", and breakdown.cooldowns repeats the same claim ("save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight"). Apprehend does not intercept a dash.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Darius sweeps up his enemies with his axe's hook and pulls them to him." It is an instant cone sweep, not a projectile with travel time and not a dash-stopper. A Darius told to hook a dash in flight will burn a 16-26s cooldown on empty air. The workable version is the reverse: pull him after Slice and Dice lands, when he has no second exit.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in tldr, report[0], breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.trading and report[11].

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late says "your R heals and executes through his empowered burst". Noxian Guillotine does not heal.
audit.why: Riot's text on R: "Darius leaps to an enemy champion and strikes a lethal blow, dealing true damage." No heal. The heal is on Decimate (Q), and only off the outer blade, and only from champions and large monsters. Telling a player his ult heals him will get him killed pressing it at low health.
audit.corrected: content.late rewritten to put the heal on Decimate where it belongs and the true damage on Guillotine.
sources: champ-data/_kits darius Q and R text

audit.whatIsWrong: Ruthless Predator is an auto-attack reset and nothing on the page says so.
audit.why: Flagged in _missing for this pairing (rule autoreset-burst-tell) and carried on the kit's W flags. It changes the read: the combo opens on an auto-attack wind-up, not on a visible ability cast, so a Darius watching for the cast animation is already stunned by the time he reacts. The tell is the wind-up.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why now states it as the level-2 fact.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cull the Meek heals off every unit hit on a flat 7-second cooldown at zero cost, and Grievous Wounds is never mentioned.
audit.why: Flagged in _missing (rule needs-antiheal). Riot's text: "heals for a small portion of the damage dealt. If he has more than 50 Fury, his damage and heal are increased." Because it is AoE and free, he refunds a trade off the minion wave between every exchange, which is the mechanism that beats Darius's chip-and-extend pattern.
audit.corrected: report[8] now buys Executioner's Calling early; the heal itself is named in whys[3], mid, spikes[2], dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.trading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's only listed defect is that the page "never names any of Renekton's abilities (Reign of Anger, Cull the Meek, Ruthless Predator, Slice and Dice, Dominus)". The content layer talks in slot letters and invented shorthand: "fury W stun", "slice-stun-slice-Q", "double-slice fury dump", "E-slice range", "his rage bar". breakdown.carry also says 7.5/10 while carryRating, breakdown.difficulty and report[14] all say 8.5/10.
audit.why: Slot letters are unreadable mid-loading-screen and the shorthand is not a real thing anyone can look up. Every named ability also carries a cooldown and a range that turns the advice into something countable.
audit.corrected: All five abilities named with their real cooldowns across early, mid, late, spikes[0..2], whys, the phases and the report entries. breakdown.carry corrected to 8.5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carries no numbers at all, and the two entries it does have are the generic Apprehend/Ghost boilerplate that appears verbatim on the Poppy and Quinn pages.
audit.why: This lane is decided by one number: Ruthless Predator is 16s at rank 1 and 8s at rank 5, and it is the only hard CC he has. Slice and Dice is 16s down to 10s. Apprehend is 26s down to 16s. Without those the advice "bait it" has nothing behind it.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with all three, plus the shield-strip consequence.
sources: champ-data/_kits renekton W cd 16/14/12/10/8, E cd 16/14.5/13/11.5/10

edits.before: Level 1 is yours — Renekton has no fury and can't empower, so a clean Q on the outer edge outdamages his auto pokes. Respect that at level 2-3 he'll build fury fast; keep minions between you and don't walk into E-slice range with a full bar.

edits.before: Levels 2-4 are Renekton's window: empowered W stuns and his double-slice fury dump beats your unstacked Hemorrhage, and his AoE heal keeps him topped. Play for CS, soak the poke, and refuse the all-in until you've got 5 stacks and level 6 online.
edits.after: Levels 2-5 are Renekton's window: an empowered Ruthless Predator stuns 1.5s and strips shields, Slice and Dice shreds your Armor, and Cull the Meek heals him off the whole wave every 7 seconds. Play for CS and refuse the all-in until 5 stacks and level 6.

edits.before: Once you hit 6 with stacks, the matchup inverts — your R heals and executes through his empowered burst, and he has no sustained answer. With first item you win every extended trade and he only scales down from here.
edits.after: Once you hit 6 with stacks the matchup inverts — Decimate's outer blade heals you, Guillotine's true damage ignores his Armor, and Dominus only delays it. With first item you win every extended trade.

edits.before: Renekton’s fury W stun and dashes dominate your early game. Don’t trade into his rage bar, bait his empowered W, and win mid-game with bleed + execute. Don't chase past the wave into Ruthless Predator (Stun).
edits.after: Ruthless Predator and Slice and Dice dominate your early game. Don't trade into a full Fury bar — bait the empowered W, which stuns 1.5s and destroys damage shields, then win the mid-game on bleed and execute.

edits.before: - Renekton Ruthless Predator (Stun): matchup-defining — Empowered = long stun. Bait it. Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane.
edits.after: - Renekton Ruthless Predator: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1 down to 8s at rank 5. Over 50 Fury it stuns 1.5s instead of 0.75s and destroys damage shields, so do not bank on a Sterak's lifeline. - Renekton Slice and Dice: 10-16s dash that shreds your Armor when empowered. - Darius Apprehend: 16-26s by rank; it cannot catch a dash in flight, so pull him after he lands.

edits.before: Good trade: Look for them to walk forward to secure a critical minion last hit. Step up instantly, land an auto-attack directly into a fast Crippling Strike (W) reset, and use the heavy slow to step back out of their counter-abilities. If they panic and waste their primary mobility or crowd control tool, activate Ghost immediately, pull them back with Apprehend, and stack your passive to full for an easy execution loop. • • Darius Top Lane Matchup Database 27 Bad trade: Whiffing Apprehend and then fighting anyway — without the pull you have no engage, and chasing through a wave bleeds you dry.
edits.after: Good trade: step up when his Fury bar is low, land an auto into a Crippling Strike reset, take the 0.75s stun, and walk out at 3-4 stacks with the Decimate heal banked. Great trade: he empties an empowered Ruthless Predator on the wave — that is 8-16 seconds without a stun, so Apprehend and commit everything. Bad trade: extending on a low Renekton, because Reign of Anger generates faster the lower he drops and Cull the Meek heals off every minion around him. Do not use Apprehend to chase Slice and Dice; it does not intercept a dash, and the whiff costs you up to 26 seconds.

notes:
NOT FIXED, needs structural repair outside the length band: full.breakdown.wave and full.report[4].t are the same ~1280-character string carrying the identical PDF scrape contamination found on the Quinn page — the headers "Key Mechanical Cooldowns" and "How Darius Wins Trades" embedded mid-paragraph, two stray bullet glyphs, and the whole cooldown block plus the whole trading block duplicated inside the wave-management text. Removing the injected blocks is roughly a 60% cut, outside the ±10% band, so I left it rather than pad it with filler. This is now confirmed on at least three darius matchups (poppy, quinn, renekton) with page numbers 27 and 62 appearing in breakdown.trading, so it is a systematic import artefact — worth grepping darius.full.js for 'Matchup Database', 'Key Mechanical Cooldowns' and the '• •' glyph pair across every enemy before the next run.

CONFIDENCE CAVEAT on one edit: dosFull[1].d asserts that Renekton's bar drains when he spends an empowered ability. Riot's kit text only says "This Fury can empower his abilities with bonus effects" — it does not state the 50-Fury consumption explicitly. I wrote it because the entire existing page already depends on it ("bait his empowered W", dosFull[1].t "Fight when his fury is empty") and because the >50 Fury threshold is stated on both Q and W, but it is the one claim here that does not come verbatim from the kit.

Kit-flag note: Darius's E carries a 'knockup' flag; Riot's text says he "pulls them to him", so I wrote pull throughout and never knockup. Renekton's Q carries a 'heal' flag described as "anti-heal target" — that flag is about Grievous Wounds being useful against him, not about him applying anti-heal, and I treated it that way.

Cross-page pattern worth the user's attention: full.diffRating was 8/10 on both Quinn and Renekton and full.breakdown.carry read 7.5/10 on both while carryRating read 8.5/10 on both. The carry-threat mismatch looks like a template bug rather than three coincidences — checking whether breakdown.carry is generated from a stale field across all darius matchups would probably fix dozens at once.
